The preceding sections established q-torsion as a geometric invariant of the brane tower and showed that the descent-eigenspace mass decomposition encodes particle identity as a knot type. We now position this within the categorical framework. A particle at a point is a knot localized at a categorical point of the projective line \mathbb{P}(V). A bundle (the physical state at the initial moment) is a finite collection of such localized knots.

This formalizes the operational bundle scenario: an initial state comprises a finite set of pairs (p_i, K_i) where p_i \in \mathbb{P}(V) and K_i is a knot type. The q-torsion drives the evolution of these positions across \mathbb{P}(V) \cong \mathbb{CP}^1, dictating the mechanical trajectories.
